outputs.summary: Added the single-card lifecycle in src/core/services/kanban/attempts.ts, tests first. playKanbanCard (kanban.play, human-only) marks a pending play in Backlog or In progress with no open attempt; it is idempotent, and returns invalid_state in Ready for review, in Done or while an attempt is open. claimKanbanCard (kanban.claim, orchestrator) returns already_claimed while an attempt is open, then invalid_state for Done, then play_required without a pending play. It consumes the play, creates attempt n+1 (ids.secret(), token <attemptId>.<secret>, ctx.machineId, 900 s default lease), moves the card to In progress and returns a KanbanPacket: card content, ctx.checkout().branch, every earlier kick-back comment in order, reporting text naming heartbeat_kanban_card, submit_kanban_card and fail_kanban_card, and ctx.definitionOfDone(). heartbeat, submit and fail (kanban.report, orchestrator and worker) check the token with the plan attempts' check, now shared as verifyClaimToken (stale_claim, expired_claim). Overdue leases are first expired in a transaction of their own, like settleLeases, so an expiry stays recorded when the report then fails. Heartbeat extends the lease by the length the claim holds; the first one moves the attempt to running. Submit uses normalizeOutputs and normalizeEvidence and moves the card to Ready for review. Fail leaves the card In progress with no pending play. expireKanbanLeases works like expireLeases: lease_expired, card stays In progress, Play allowed again. Play, claim and the reports run it, and so do listKanbanCards and getKanbanCard in the command layer (swept, as in commands/checkpoints.ts), so the board shows the expiry and Play reappears. approveKanbanCard (kanban.review, human-only) accepts the attempt and moves the card to Done. It sets completed_at and compacted_at, and summary_json gets {outcome: the summary on one line, cut to 280 characters with an ellipsis and never splitting a surrogate pair; commits; completedAt; approvedBy}. kickBackKanbanCard (kanban.review) requires a non-blank comment of at most LIMITS.comment characters. It rejects the attempt with review_comment and returns the card to In progress with a pending play. Every transition writes a kanban_events row with attempt_id and a workspace event kanban.<kind> carrying {cardId, key, attemptId?} and no epic. Kinds: played, claimed, running, submitted, failed, lease_expired, approved, kicked_back. The payloads carry what DM-381 needs: number, machineId and leaseExpiresAt, outputs and evidence, reason, comment, summary. Later heartbeats with a note append only a kanban.progress workspace event. Registration: COMMAND_SCHEMAS (strict zod: leaseSeconds 30..86400, progressNote at most LIMITS.progressNote, the submitAttempt outputs and evidence schemas, commentBody for the comment, idempotencyKey on claim, submit, fail, approve and kick back), commands/kanban.ts, COMMAND_CAPABILITIES, CommandApi and input types in shared/domain/api.ts, DESKTOP_COMMANDS (play, approve, kick back), stubApi, the capability probe matrix, the MCP inventory test, and AGENT_ONLY_COMMANDS in handlers.test.ts. New error code: play_required (invalid_state and already_claimed already existed; card_not_owned belongs to DM-381 and is not added). Adaptations: (1) The packet has no epic intent; I read the Contract from the plan snapshot in the worktree's .darkmechanicus, without editing it. (2) cards.ts now exports SummaryRow, AttemptRow, toAttemptView, loadSummaryRow, cardView and recordCardEvent. recordCardEvent takes the event as one object {kind, payload, attemptId?} because the lint limit is 4 parameters, and both DM-379 callers were migrated. (3) Reuse instead of copies: plan verifyClaim now delegates to verifyClaimToken (same checks, same order, same errors); heartbeatIntervalSeconds, normalizeOutputs, normalizeEvidence and maskNote are exported from services/attempts.ts; guardUnique guards the one-open-attempt index. (4) Security fix found by the red-team review: claimTokenMask recognised only at_ tokens. It now recognises the ka_ tokens of Kanban attempts too (TOKEN_START, TOKEN_TAIL), which covers chats, storedSecrets and idempotency. Kanban reports (outputs, evidence, reason) mask the token, its bare secret and any other whole token with maskWholeClaimTokens, so a path like docs/at_<id>.json survives. Progress notes use maskNote plus the bare secret. (5) The authz DESKTOP filter became an AGENT_ONLY list for the complexity lint; the resulting sets are the same plus the Kanban changes. Fixed after the first round:
- (a) A card's exports deadlocked when the checkout held a card.json of a later generation.

The second round found no new blocker or major problem. Survived both rounds: secret masking (tokens and bare secrets in notes, outputs, evidence, comments and reasons), path containment (links, junctions, non-id names, temp files, directories where files belong), event immutability, same-millisecond ordering, card_not_owned ordering, the db-mode no-write guarantee, and the epic seams.

Known limits:
- (1) Card conflicts are recorded, but the flush that follows every heartbeat reconcile clears them as soon as the local export wins, so the storage status rarely shows one. The desktop does not render kanbanConflicts yet, and UI is out of scope.
- (2) A Play pressed on another computer between a claim and the attempt's close, before that computer saw the claim, is dropped by design. Clock skew larger than the sync delay can drop a later Play too. Event times compare as text, which is correct for the app's own `.sssZ` stamps only.

Kanban cards are now portable records in repo mode, and only SQLite rows in db mode. Tests were written first: the new files failed for the right reasons before the implementation.

What changed:
- Layout: RepoLayout.kanbanDir is created by ownedDirs in repo mode only. ownedPaths gains kanbanCardDir, kanbanCardFile (kanban/<cardId>/card.json), kanbanEventsDir and kanbanEventFile (kanban/<cardId>/events/<eventId>.json). Every segment goes through checkedId, and assertContained guards every read and write.
- Records (portable.ts): kanbanCardRecord (darkmechanicus.kanban-card v1) holds the definition, key, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt and generation. kanbanEventRecord (darkmechanicus.kanban-event v1) is a strict discriminated union per kind: id, cardId, kind, attemptId, actor, payload, createdAt. buildKanbanCardRecord, readKanbanEventRecord and buildKanbanEventRecord build them, and trackedKanbanCardHash and trackedKanbanEventHash hash them. The event builder masks every claim secret of the card's attempts and any whole claim token, as defense in depth.
- Outbox: OutboxKind and ExportKind gain kanban_card and kanban_event. recordCardEvent enqueues kanban_event for every event, and kanban_card on created and updated only, in the same transaction.
- Finalizer, repo mode:
  - card.json is written at the next generation, and only over the record this machine last exported or imported, or one a reconcile reported as a conflict with a local edit (noted as seen). Any other tracked card.json makes the entry fail with conflict until a reconcile has reported it.
  - Event files are written once by writeOnce, the comment writer generalised. An existing file with different content is a conflict and is left unchanged. Records are capped at MAX_RECORD_BYTES.
  - An event waits while its card's card.json is not in the checkout.
- Finalizer, db mode: DB_HANDLERS settle both kinds without a file or a sync_state row.
- Seams:
  - entityKeys returns kanban:<cardId>; queuedAfter computes card_id for both kinds.
  - An epic-scoped flush skips the kanban kinds.
  - hasPendingEpicChanges and conflictsOf exclude them.
  - StorageStatusView and ReconcileResultView gain kanbanConflicts {cardId, message}.
- Import (new src/core/repo/kanbanImport.ts, wired into reconcileRepository; db mode stays a no-op):
  - It scans kanban/ with contained readers. A bad file rejects its whole card.
  - It applies changed card definitions, unless a local edit is pending: that is a conflict, the local card is kept, and the tracked hash and generation are noted as seen.
  - It inserts new events. An event already held here with other content is a conflict.
  - It rebuilds each card's lane, attempts (state, outputs, evidence, review comment, timestamps), pending Play and Done summary from the ordered event stream.
  - An imported attempt keeps its machine id and gets an unusable random secret.
- Lifecycle: heartbeat, submit and fail on another computer's attempt return card_not_owned, checked before the token. expireKanbanLeases expires only this computer's attempts. Transitions pass their own time to recordCardEvent, so event times equal the row times and a rebuild matches exactly.
